query: Explain how `dumppdf` in `tools/dumppdf.py` decides what to dump from a PDF file: how object ids, page numbers, the dump-all option and the codec interact, what `dumpallobjs` and `dumptrailers` contribute, and how fallback cross-reference tables and missing objects are handled.

operations.name: Requested object ids are fetched from the document and dumped as XML
For selected pages a codec dumps the page content streams, otherwise the page attributes
The dump-all option dumps every object in the document
With nothing requested only the trailers are dumped
expressions: if (not objids) and (not pagenos) and (not dumpall):

operations.name: The full dump skips objects it has already seen and reports objects that cannot be found

dependencies.name: A trailing newline is written unless the codec is raw or binary
Trailers of fallback cross-reference tables are shown only on request
expressions: if not isinstance(xref, PDFXRefFallback) or show_fallback_xref:

dependencies.name: A warning is logged when the file has no real cross-reference table and fallback tables are hidden
expressions: no_xrefs = all(isinstance(xref, PDFXRefFallback) for xref in doc.xrefs)

dependencies.name: The full dump is wrapped in a pdf element and ends with the trailers
